hints.title: 1 · Choose a bounded example
hints.body: Pick one situation where your actions and the stakes are clear. A smaller honest example is more useful than an invented dramatic one.

hints.title: 2 · Separate decisions from chronology
hints.body: Name your responsibility, the alternatives you considered, what you actually did, and who else contributed. Explain why each important action mattered.

hints.title: 3 · Close with evidence and reflection
hints.body: State what you observed afterward and how you know. If the result was mixed or uncertain, explain that limitation and what you changed next time.

criteria.title: Clear situation and stakes
criteria.target: Give enough context, constraints and stakes to understand the decision without an unrelated chronology.
criteria.probe: What context can you remove without changing the listener’s understanding?
criteria.practice: Give the opening in two sentences: problem, stakes, and your responsibility.

criteria.title: Specific personal contribution
criteria.target: Distinguish your actions and decisions from team outcomes, including how you involved others.
criteria.probe: Which action was specifically yours, and what did someone else contribute?
criteria.practice: Replace vague “we” statements with precise personal actions while crediting collaborators.

criteria.title: Tradeoffs and accountability
criteria.target: Explain real alternatives, constraints, risk ownership, a review trigger, and observed outcomes without presenting the decision as risk-free.
criteria.probe: Which assumption would have changed your decision?
criteria.practice: Compare two viable alternatives using the constraints you actually faced and one explicit revisit trigger.

criteria.title: Outcomes, limits and reflection
criteria.target: Explain observed results, attribution limits, and what you would repeat or change without inventing evidence.
criteria.probe: What did you learn that changed your behavior on a later occasion?
criteria.practice: State an observable outcome, its evidence limit and one concrete behavior you changed.

follow_up: How would you handle evidence that the chosen shortcut was costing more than expected while delivery pressure remained high?
